acceptance_criteria.criterion: PHPRenderer generates method code matching the current output format in Icon.php (except the region label change).
JSRenderer generates method code matching the current output format in icon.js.
The PHP region label is "// region: Icon methods" (not "Icon type methods").
Both classes compile without errors and pass PHPStan.

summary: Created PHPRenderer (src/classes/Application/Composer/IconBuilder/PHPRenderer.php) extending AbstractLanguageRenderer. Renders PHP icon accessor methods with docblock in the format: `public function {camelCase}() : self { return $this->setType(...); }`. Method name is the icon ID converted to camelCase via lcfirst(toPascalCase()).

Created JSRenderer (src/classes/Application/Composer/IconBuilder/JSRenderer.php) extending AbstractLanguageRenderer. Renders JS icon accessor methods in the format: `{PascalCase}:function() { return this.SetType(...); },`. Method name is the icon ID converted to PascalCase via toPascalCase().

Both classes use `array()` syntax, declare(strict_types=1), no constructor promotion. Both inherit the unified REGION_LABEL ('Icon methods') from AbstractLanguageRenderer, satisfying the region label AC.

Verified output format against actual Icon.php and icon.js: all 6 format checks pass (region label, no-prefix method, with-prefix method for both languages). 213 icons loaded from the framework icons.json.
Ran composer dump-autoload to register new classes in the classmap. PHPStan analysis shows only the pre-existing DBHelper/FetchMany.php error — no new issues introduced. IconsTest passes.

comments.note: The renderSetTypeArgs() helper is duplicated identically in both PHPRenderer and JSRenderer. A protected method on AbstractLanguageRenderer could eliminate this duplication. Out of scope for this WP but worth noting for a future cleanup.

vendor/shark/simple_html_dom/simple_html_dom.php emits PHP 8.4 deprecation notices for $http_response_header on lines 99, 102, and 113. This is a pre-existing third-party dependency issue unrelated to this WP.

summary: Independently verified PHPRenderer and JSRenderer output format by instantiating both classes against the live icons.json (214 icons). All 10 format checks passed: region label, no-prefix method, with-prefix method, camelCase ID handling, and endregion marker — for both languages.
PHPStan analysis confirmed no new errors introduced. The single existing error (DBHelper/FetchMany.php) is pre-existing and unrelated to this WP.
IconsTest regression check passed (2/2 assertions). Edge-case scan of all 214 icons confirmed no reserved PHP words as IDs and no single-quote or backslash characters in icon names or types.
Both renderer classes: correct use of array() syntax, declare(strict_types=1), no constructor promotion — consistent with project conventions.

comments.note: renderSetTypeArgs() is duplicated identically in both PHPRenderer and JSRenderer. Moving it to AbstractLanguageRenderer as a protected method would eliminate duplication. This is a forward-looking observation — the logic is correct as-is, no impact on current AC.

No edge-case risks found: 214 icons checked, none have reserved PHP keywords as IDs and none contain special characters (single quotes, backslashes) in icon name or type fields. The renderers are safe against the current icon dataset.

summary: PHPRenderer and JSRenderer reviewed — clean, well-structured Template Method pattern. One Fix-Forward applied: moved the identical renderSetTypeArgs() helper from both subclasses into AbstractLanguageRenderer as a protected method, eliminating the DRY violation flagged by both Developer and QA. Output format verified; IconsTest continues to pass (2/2). All acceptance criteria confirmed met.

comments.note: Moved renderSetTypeArgs(IconDefinition $icon) : string from private methods in PHPRenderer and JSRenderer into AbstractLanguageRenderer as a protected method. The two implementations were byte-for-byte identical; this is a non-behavioral refactor that satisfies DRY. Both subclasses now inherit the method. IconsTest (2/2) confirms output is unchanged.

The render() method in AbstractLanguageRenderer emits lines with trailing whitespace ('    ' . PHP_EOL) to preserve target-file structure. This is intentional and format-verified, but worth flagging for any future linter integration that strips trailing spaces before insertion.

[documentation-forward] AbstractLanguageRenderer.renderSetTypeArgs() is now a protected shared method but its docblock says 'setType() / SetType()' to accommodate both callers. The module documentation should note this shared helper when documenting the renderer architecture.
